name: British Plexi-style 50 W (jumpered)
notes: Late-60s British 50 W style, normal and bright channels jumpered, both volumes at 7. Path: two V1 triodes in parallel (bright channel has the bright cap) -> 470k mixing resistors -> V2a -> cathode follower -> tone stack (no master volume) -> phase inverter -> 2x EL34 with feedback and presence. FROM SCHEMATICS (fairly sure): 12AX7 stages with 100k plate resistors, tone stack 22n/22n/33k slope/1M bass/25k mid, EL34 pair into 3.4k, presence in the feedback loop. UNSURE / APPROXIMATED: bright cap as a +8 dB shelf at 1.5 kHz; 470k mixing resistors as -6 dB plus a 5 kHz low-pass (Miller capacitance of V2a); V2a partial cathode bypass as a -4 dB shelf below 300 Hz; the cathode follower clipping as a custom curve (top 40 V); treble cap 500 pF; bias voltages of the preamp stages; feedback amount (set for about 7 dB of feedback); phase inverter as one triode that gets half the input (each triode of the real long-tailed pair sees half the signal, so it has twice the headroom of a single stage). MEASURED LIMIT: it does not clean up much when played softly (about 32% harmonics at 0.05 V input). The preamp is clean then (2% up to the tone stack); the distortion comes from the phase inverter and power amp, which get about 17 V from the tone stack because there is no master volume. Whether the real amp does this at volume 7 needs a comparison with a recording of a real one. POWER SUPPLY: silicon rectifier: only the transformer winding, as 80 ohm into 50 uF (supply_ohms, supply_uf on the power block), so the sag comes from the current the power tubes really draw. These two values are GUESSES from typical parts, not from this amp's schematic. (It replaced a sag block.)
